# DECISIONS.md

Preserve historical ADR numbers and concise, public design rationale; omit private samples, deployment records, and dates.
Accepted identifies the current design choice, not validation in every environment. See [KNOWN_RISKS](KNOWN_RISKS.md) for gaps.
New decisions describe context, choice/reason, alternatives/cost, and review conditions. Mark supersession explicitly;
never silently overwrite an existing constraint.

## ADR-001: Memory / MemoryBackend boundary (Accepted)

Hosts need replaceable storage. Keep the public storage API in `Memory`, constrain backends with a Protocol, and lazy-load them.
This avoids upper-layer SQL and optional-dependency coupling. Cost: both backends must maintain the same contract;
review parity when extending an API.

## ADR-002: RawEvent is evidence for derived memory (Accepted)

L0 is append-only; Candidates/AtomCards retain raw references and verbatim quotations for tracing and re-extraction.
Model rewrites do not replace valuable originals. Cost: evidence storage and privacy retention require separate management;
review them when changing retention.

## ADR-003: Extractor has no persistence side effects (Accepted)

`CandidateExtractor.extract()` returns results; its caller decides persistence. LLM/parse failures return `failure_reason`.
This supports tests, inspection, and retries, but callers must distinguish failure from a successful empty result.
The extractor currently calls the model in batches and stops at the first failed batch. Only after the entire extraction
pass succeeds does Runtime atomically commit candidates and the `extracted_ids/v1/<session>` cursor, then advance memory state.
Runtime does not persist partial successes batch by batch; candidate/cursor write failures roll back together.
See [extraction and durable progress](PROJECT_MAP.md#extraction-and-durable-progress) for budgets and downstream-stage boundaries.

## ADR-004: Rule-first promotion (Accepted)

Run value → evidence → entity → duplicate → conflict checks; the first terminal outcome wins. Escalate ambiguity to an LLM.
This avoids a model call per candidate. Cost: jointly validate rules and state mapping; review the demotion-only boundary
when adding automatic promotion conditions.

## ADR-005: Append and deprecate facts (Accepted)

Create a new atom and invalidate the old one through `superseded_by`/`deprecated_at`; default queries exclude invalid facts.
Do not overwrite assertions in place, preserving relationships and auditability. Cost: historical storage and concurrent
replacement control. Manual correction is covered by ADR-034.

## ADR-006: Store EntityPage separately (Accepted)

Separate entity and page tables. Pages track dirty/version/regeneration state, retain old content on failure, and preserve `## My Notes`.
This keeps large bodies out of hot indexes and protects user notes from generation. Cost: asynchronous updates may be stale;
review that behavior when changing regeneration.

## ADR-007: Independent notes tree (Superseded by ADR-010)

Previously, tree facts and pipeline facts were separate and tree leaves were an independent recall source.
The single-fact-source design replaces this arrangement; it is not a current implementation rule.

## ADR-008: Host shells reuse the Python runtime (Accepted)

OpenClaw uses TypeScript plus a stdio JSON-RPC bridge; Hermes reuses Bridge handlers in-process.
Avoid a second memory algorithm implementation or an extra network daemon. Cost: validate interpreter, process,
and protocol lifecycles; see the [integration guide](../integrations.md).

## ADR-009: Versioned JSONL migration (Accepted)

A first-line header, record envelopes, and dependency order enable streaming import/export instead of copying backend-private SQL data.
Cost: new fields and format upgrades need explicit compatibility rules. Revisit when changing export/import.

## ADR-010: AtomCard is the canonical fact (Accepted; supersedes ADR-007)

Leaves store only `atom_id`; reads JOIN the atom assertion. Manual store, promotion, and direct atom writes share one fact chain.
Entities map to organization branches; tree is no longer a recall source. This avoids duplicate fact writes, at the cost of
leaf lifecycle depending on atoms. See current source conditions in [PROJECT_MAP](PROJECT_MAP.md);
do not reuse the historical absolute claim that recall has only atom/raw sources.

## ADR-011: Host supplies hybrid context (Accepted; real-host validation pending)

Before prompt construction, OpenClaw invokes the optional `recallPrefetcher`; the synchronous promptBuilder consumes its result.
Do not try to supply this turn's context from `agent_end`. Cost: actual host hook invocation is required;
review it when upgrading the SDK/host.

## ADR-012: Capture supports short CJK text and strips think blocks (Accepted)

Shared capture policy uses CJK-weighted length and strips `<think>` before length checks and storage.
Explicit intent keywords no longer admit short messages; agents call memory_save for deliberate saves.
This avoids duplicated host filters and re-ingestion of reasoning. Cost: boundary-length messages can be filtered;
validate multilingual samples when changing thresholds.

## ADR-021: Layered directories and shared MemoryRuntime (Accepted)

Use adapters → application → pipeline/core/storage/ports/domain. Service must not depend on bridge, nor storage on pipeline.
Do not retain shims for old internal paths, avoiding two long-lived layouts. Cost: internal import users must migrate.
Define any future stable extension API separately; this decision does not authorize breaking existing public APIs.

## ADR-022: Checkpoint pruning is separate from memory GC (Accepted; safety extended by ADR-029/036)

Separate execution-state cleanup from fact lifecycle. Do not add a journal row per deletion and grow one table while clearing another.
Cost: independent statistics and restore-dependency checks. Row deletion, history pruning, and physical reclamation are distinct.

## ADR-023: Merge extract_run heartbeats (Superseded by ADR-028)

The historical approach merged quiet journal entries by session. Current code overwrites meta;
heartbeat configuration no longer controls journal writes.

## ADR-024: Partial indexes for SQLite journal targets (Accepted)

Targets are usually null. Use `WHERE col IS NOT NULL` and idempotent schema-introspection migration, without adding columns or tables.
Query semantics stay unchanged. Cost: rebuilding old indexes takes time; revisit coverage when changing journal queries.

## ADR-025: Intent-oriented space maintenance APIs (Accepted)

`check_storage` diagnoses read-only, `nudge_vacuum` reclaims lightly, and `compact_vacuum` performs heavy maintenance,
with backend-specific implementations. Callers need not depend on engine terminology.
Cost: locking, space, and shared-table scope differ; ordinary PG VACUUM also cannot promise no lock waits.

## ADR-026: Raw is fallback by default (Superseded for automatic injection by ADR-044)

With explicit multi-source retrieval, recall applies `raw_policy=fallback`: durable results prevent raw top-ups,
and current-session/thread raw is excluded. This avoids echoing the active conversation into prompts,
at the cost of possibly fewer results. Tools can explicitly select raw policy; review filter order when changing it.

## ADR-027: Hosts schedule light maintenance while idle (Accepted)

New SQLite files use INCREMENTAL. `run_idle_maintenance()` runs prune → gc → nudge.
Heavy compaction and WAL truncation need an appropriate idle window and space checks.
The library does not promise every host schedules them automatically; validate host wiring separately.

## ADR-028: Separate runtime summaries from decision journals (Accepted; supersedes ADR-023)

`extract_run` overwrites a meta summary; journal retention depends on action, and GC returns counts rather than per-row entries.
This prevents idle activity from inflating the audit table. Cost: summaries cannot replay every empty pass;
see the risk list for the PG retention gap.

## ADR-029: Seal parent graphs before pruning (Accepted)

Keep stepwise checkpoints within a turn. Pruning defaults to `keep_last=1`: seal parent-graph messages first,
then delete ancestors/subgraphs under safety checks. In-progress, HITL, or failed-sealing cases are not ordinary completed turns.
Cost: sealing and dependency-validation work; review it when changing restore semantics.

## ADR-030: Short transactions for ordinary PostgreSQL operations (Accepted)

End ordinary read/write transactions through `_cursor()`; explicit transactions preserve atomicity across operations.
Bootstrap uses lock timeouts and an FTS catalog fast path. This avoids idle transactions blocking DDL.
Cost: genuinely long migrations need separate planning rather than globally relaxed timeouts.

## ADR-031: Manual adoption is a user decision (Accepted)

Pending candidates run automatic checks. Approval handles conflict/needs_review; duplicates merge,
and a successor replaces contradictory active atoms. Fact writes, candidate state, supersession, and user journal share one transaction.
Cost: this explicitly overrides automatic judgment and must not be treated as an ordinary retry.

## ADR-032: Recover PostgreSQL connections at cursor boundaries (Superseded by ADR-040)

Reset/reconnect and restore search_path only outside transactions; a failed explicit transaction stays failed.
Avoid silently committing partial work. Cost: callers retry the whole transaction.
The existing SQLite-only GC gap does not authorize silent backend capability divergence.

## ADR-033: Namespace-first GIN (Accepted)

In the shared PG schema, try `btree_gin` plus `GIN(namespace, tsv)`. Attempt extension installation inside a savepoint;
failure retains ordinary GIN. Queries remain correct without permission to install the extension.
Cost: weaker namespace performance isolation; use real PG validation.

## ADR-034: Manual correction appends an atom (Accepted)

The successor retains historical provenance and `user_edit` records the correction; do not fabricate a RawEvent/Candidate.
Both backends require active-only supersession and complete rollback on failure.
Cost: the original quote is provenance, not evidence proving the corrected assertion.

## ADR-035: Aware UTC for absolute Episode times (Accepted)

Normalize write/read/query boundaries to UTC; interpret legacy naive values as UTC and defensively normalize sorting.
This avoids mixed datetime types without requiring upfront migration.
Cost: unknown historical local time zones cannot be recovered; future local-time support needs a separate field and versioned migration.

## ADR-036: Reuse checkpoint content with explicit migration (Accepted)

SQLite uses same-database typed blobs and a format envelope to reuse large fields. Reads restore historical values,
not the latest workspace file. Separate new writes from historical migration; independent readers have their own decoder/cache.
Cost: old readers are incompatible, so expand before downgrade.
See [checkpoint maintenance](../../CONTRIBUTING.md#checkpoint-maintenance) for offline migration, backups, and rollback.

`db slim` previews by default; explicit apply/offline creates a backup, deduplicates, and reclaims space without implicit history pruning.
Advanced options remain under checkpoints. For online slimming, the host pauses new invocations, coordinates readers,
and resumes. Batches are transactional and do not chase an unlimited stream of new rows.
Long readers can postpone WAL reclamation. Keep backups and report partial completion;
never overwrite subsequent legitimate writes automatically with a backup.

## ADR-037: Unified Octop naming with stable disk protocols (Accepted)

The distribution/CLI is `octop-memory`, Python package `octop_memory`, and plugin ID `octopmemory`.
Rename environment variables, default paths, bridge probe fields, and the PG schema together, without old-entry aliases.
SQLite checkpoint encoding, `hm_*` tables, and `.hmpkg` are persistent protocols and remain stable to protect historical reads.
Cost: old installations explicitly migrate configuration, directories, or PG schema; maintain those steps only in the
[integration guide](../integrations.md#renaming-and-migrating-existing-installations).

## ADR-038: Degrade only on expected driver and I/O failures (Accepted)

Queries, files, and timeouts use `storage/driver_errors.py`'s `DRIVER_ERRORS`
(`sqlite3.Error`, installed `psycopg.Error`, `OSError`, `TimeoutError`, `RuntimeError`), log warnings, and degrade.
Vector indexes use `VECTOR_ERRORS`. Doctor, extraction boundaries, bridge, idle maintenance, backfill, and host polling use `REPORTABLE_ERRORS`.
Transaction rollback and checkpoint-backup deletion use `try`/`finally`; failures and cancellation roll back.
Exceptions outside the relevant tuples propagate. `AssertionError` is not a degradation exception.

## ADR-039: One SQLite connection per backend, serialized operations and transactions (Accepted)

Remove thread-local connection registries so multiple agents and permanent workers do not multiply connections.
Each backend has one `check_same_thread=False` connection and a reentrant lock covering execute/fetch/commit,
explicit transactions, and close. Failed writes outside explicit transactions roll back and re-raise the original error.
Internal vacuum, WAL truncation, and export SQL use the same protection, preventing maintenance from interleaving in normal transactions.

Choose one connection rather than a SQLite pool to reduce idle file descriptors and lifecycle branches.
PG pooling is covered by ADR-040. Cost: slow queries and long transactions block other SQL on the same backend.
LLM calls stay outside those operation locks; different backends and the separate checkpoint connection can still run concurrently.
SQLite/WAL, tables, atomicity, and recall contracts are unchanged, with no data migration.
Future same-backend SQL concurrency needs bounded leases and renewed transaction/closure validation.

## ADR-040: Bounded PostgreSQL pools shared by connection configuration (Accepted)

One business connection plus a checkpoint pool per agent still compounds capacity: 69 active agents need at least
138 sessions; ten-minute idle release cannot cover active peaks. Share 8 business and 4 checkpoint/maintenance connections
per process, normalized DSN, and driver options. Namespace stays in SQL predicates, not pool identity.
Distinct session settings use separate pools to avoid mixing identity/configuration.

A business lease covers the complete cursor/result/transaction. Explicit transactions retain one connection and the backend's
reentrant lock across calls. Checkout detects bad connections; return commits or rolls back. Do not reconnect later writes
inside a broken transaction. Pool configuration restores search_path. psycopg_pool reclamation, liveness checks, and reconnect
backoff replace the private persistent `_conn`, per-instance idle Timer, and reconnect cooldown.
The `postgres` extra explicitly includes psycopg-pool, already used by checkpoints, rather than implementing another pool.

LangGraph requires ConnectionPool. An internal lease adapter subclasses that type without opening its own pool,
delegates `connection()` to the shared pool, and exposes the same idempotent lease through saver.conn and
Memory._checkpointer_pool to tolerate two host close calls. Each lease releases one reference, waits for its in-flight work,
and closes the real pool only after the last reference. Checkpoint setup is serialized once per pool;
failed setup publishes neither saver nor lease and releases resources. Autovacuum settings and maintenance also use pooled connections.

Each pool allows at most 64 waiters and a 30-second checkout timeout, with `min_size=0` and `max_idle=600`.
Capacity exhaustion errors rather than opening unlimited connections or replaying potentially committed writes.
This is a per-process boundary; other processes/configurations and the host control plane need separate capacity.
Schema, encoding, recall order, and namespace contracts are unchanged. Real PG regression covers 69 agents, transactions/isolation,
saturation/recovery, idle/bad connections, initialization failure, and closure references; SQLite retains shared public-behavior assertions.

## ADR-041: Isolate runtime diagnostics by provenance, protect user knowledge (Accepted)

A runtime failure is not automatically durable knowledge. octop-harness/Octop use `on_failure="error"` to retain model failures
as checkpoint errors, displayed separately by the host; automatic team-failure notifications are excluded from capture.
Hosts still synthesizing error replies mark `payload.octop_runtime_error=true`. Capture, Candidate/Episode extractors,
promotion, and raw prompt recall exclude only structured error provenance. Remove intent/value keyword lists;
agents decide when to call memory_save. Manual writes, approvals, and edits are protected by provenance;
the extraction model judges ordinary conversation's long-term value.
**⚠️ Recall/write path change:** background capture no longer admits short messages through intent exceptions.
Even apply-mode historical governance only soft-deactivates automatic records whose evidence is entirely marked errors.
Legacy fixed retry-failure text only produces operations review hints. Missing/mixed provenance keeps state and returns review_*_ids.
Do not infer provenance from wording, delete raw evidence, or add a schema for this.

## ADR-042: Manual-document priority, conflict candidates, snapshot-bound deduplication (Accepted)

Host users maintain USER.md/MEMORY.md; the existing unified chat loader reads their full text only when a session first loads.
Memory receives current files for governance, not file writing or prompt refresh. Hosts may explicitly reconcile after saving documents.
Ordinary `MemoryService.save()` only notifies a nonblocking scheduler and does not call the comparison model synchronously.
A host worker/maintenance tick calls `review_new_memory(max_atoms=20)` and reads the provider's current documents.
Extraction/promotion does not start synchronous reconciliation.
**⚠️ Recall/write path change:** only high-confidence, mutually exclusive facts in the same subject/field/time scope,
with genuine complete source quotations, can atomically soft-deactivate an old atom, create a replacement Candidate, and journal it.
Keep original evidence; unreviewed replacements do not promote. Old conflicting raw is excluded from automatic fallback;
dirty pages wait for regeneration. Do not force changes for historical events, normal troubleshooting knowledge,
different contexts, or contradictions between the two manual documents themselves.

Keep duplicate atoms; suppress recall only when the actual session snapshot contains the same information.
Do not inject a new file version into an old session. Metadata stores reconciliation versions and audit snapshots;
a separate small manifest participates in recall cache keys so old cache entries cannot revive suppressed content.
Report model failure, uncertainty, fabricated evidence, version changes, and limits explicitly; each call can resume up to 100 new atoms.
Store compared hashes separately from unresolved `uncertain` hashes. Without the legacy unresolved dictionary, checked progress
cannot establish a conclusion: perform one bounded re-audit instead of guessing complete. Reads calculate pending work without writes;
after the first reconciliation writes the new format, retain progress. Cost: even old complete reports may need extra model comparisons.
An explicit empty unresolved dictionary is valid new-format state and must not be invalidated merely because it is falsy.
Adoption checks the last reconciliation version; supplying current documents also catches changes not yet reconciled.
Reuse Service/Bridge/retention/promotion/recall and the existing backend contract, without a new schema, full-text document index,
or separate loader. Shared SQLite/real-PG tests cover transactions, idempotency, evidence retention, and prompt filtering.

## ADR-043: Conditional page writeback using a separate mutation revision (Accepted)

`summary_version` changes with successful generation/manual edits and cannot detect new facts on an already dirty page;
timestamps may also match. Storage manages `mutation_version`, atomically incremented on body writes and dirty invalidation,
without changing summary_version semantics. Regeneration ensures a stub exists, then reads revision, notes, and atoms;
model calls run outside database transactions.
Success and failure writebacks compare the snapshot revision in the same UPDATE. A stale result must not overwrite newer content,
clear new dirty state, or increase a newer page's failure count. Failure bookkeeping does not advance the revision:
its retry count/dirty state does not change generation input, so an otherwise valid concurrent result can still commit.
Once a success advances the revision, a late failure is rejected by its original condition.
Log stale generated results as `page_regen_failed: stale_snapshot`; retry in a later explicit/dirty-batch call, not an unbounded inner loop.
A failed conditional update must not fall back to unconditional upsert. Manual edits, repeated dirty invalidation,
other successful generations, and low-level upserts advance the revision. Upsert does not assign the revision supplied in EntityPage;
imports establish revisions in the destination store.
Both SQLite/PG schema 2 add a default-zero column and migrate existing pages. SQLite checks/adds the column inside a short
BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction, serializing first migrations across connections. PG checks inside an initialization transaction-level
advisory lock and ALTERs only if missing, avoiding an exclusive lock for no-op DDL. No production dependency is added.
When no version condition is supplied, Memory keeps the legacy backend call signature. Conditional calls require custom backends
to implement the new parameter, maintain revisions, and compare atomically. Never catch TypeError and retry without a condition.
The scope is writers honoring the existing dirty contract; this does not add governance to low-level atom SQL bypassing dirty
invalidation, or promise that page journals and body commits share a transaction.


## ADR-044: Canonical atoms only for automatic injection (Accepted; supersedes ADR-026 for injection)

Raw fallback can inject casual conversation when there is no useful promoted fact. Restrict automatic recall at source gathering
to atom and optional vector atom hits; no match returns empty. Raw, page headlines, episodes, and host files remain available
through explicit search where supported, with existing raw policies and current-session exclusion. Add no model call or schema change.

`recall_for_prompt` defaults to `atom_only=True`; explicit tools pass False. OpenClaw hybrid prefetch sends `atomOnly: true`
and filters externally supplied results at prefetch/render boundaries. Service and Hermes use the pipeline default. Cache scope
includes source mode, raw policy, session, and manual snapshots, preventing a broader cached search from entering an automatic prompt.

Cost: unextracted history is no longer automatically surfaced, particularly for Hermes capture-only hooks. Low-value atoms and
topic mismatch still need separate relevance/value work; do not treat this source restriction as a semantic relevance classifier.
Review admission/ranking with positive and negative queries before adding model-assisted filtering.

## ADR-045: Caller-selected explicit-save kinds (Accepted; unreleased)

Explicit remember requests bypass automatic extraction; hardcoding every manual Candidate as Fact loses preferences,
decisions, and tasks. Add optional kind to Memory.store/MemoryService.save and preserve it as candidate_type.
The host's current conversation model selects Fact/Preference/Decision/Task in its existing tool call; no separate
classifier, keyword heuristics, schema migration, or historical backfill. Omission keeps Fact for old callers.
Reject ConflictCandidate direct promotion and non-Fact directory kinds. Keep topic/entity type independent,
and preserve evidence, user provenance, transactional writes, and nonblocking review scheduling.

Cost: callers must select an appropriate kind, and old hosts still produce Fact. Harness advertises the enum and
bilingual guidance; unsupported memory versions fail typed saves explicitly without downgrading. Release/adopt the
library API before consumer releases; local-source tests do not establish release availability. Review classification
quality using real requests; any offline reclassification of historical records needs a separate preview and scope.

## Writes, extraction, and review

- The 20,000-character extraction budget estimates content plus overhead; it is not a strict prompt/token limit.
  An oversized event still forms its own batch and can exceed model limits. Runtime reads at most 10,000 session
  raw events per call, not necessarily all history. Any model-batch failure prevents all candidate/cursor commits
  for that pass, so retries can repeat model cost. Promotion, pages, and Episodes run after that commit;
  the cursor is not an all-stages-success marker. See extraction checks in TEST_MATRIX.
- Low-level `extract_session(..., persist=True)` persists returned partial candidates without checking the overall
  `failure_reason` and does not maintain the Runtime cursor. Hosts needing incremental rollback semantics use
  Service/Bridge extract; direct extractor callers inspect the result before persisting it.
- EntityPage revision protection depends on every writer maintaining mutation_version. Upgrade all writing processes;
  old processes or direct SQL bypassing revisions/dirty invalidation do not have the same guarantee.
  Legacy page APIs without a version condition retain their old backend call form. Custom backends used for automatic
  regeneration must implement conditional parameters and revision maintenance; never ignore a guard or retry unconditionally.
  Rejected stale results are not immediately retried. Hosts later trigger dirty pages; newer clean user/generated pages stay clean.
- Background manual-document review requires a nonblocking host scheduler/provider and a worker/maintenance call to
  `MemoryService.review_new_memory`. The entry point is available from 1.0.3; a host upgrade retaining memory 1.0.2
  lacks it and skips review. Raise the host's minimum dependency. The method synchronously calls the model and must
  not return to the user-facing save path.
- Semantic reconciliation needs an auxiliary model. Only exact source quotations, explicit subject/scope, and high-confidence
  conclusions can deactivate facts; failures/uncertainty do not. Calls inspect at most 100 unchecked atoms and 100,000 document
  characters. Hosts must expose partial/uncertain/unavailable states and continuation. Without a provider, external hosts only
  reconcile explicitly. Concurrent file updates require a host freshness callback. Adoption should supply current documents;
  the lower-level worker at least checks the last reconciliation version. Old-version candidates remain auditable but cannot be
  adopted directly: reject and reconcile the new version. Conflicting raw events are excluded wholesale from automatic fallback;
  other mixed facts remain reachable through valid atoms/direct evidence reads. Historical Episodes are not bulk-deleted. See ADR-042.
- Legacy audit metadata without an `uncertain` dictionary needs one conservative re-audit, including records previously reported
  complete. Old progress cannot distinguish comparison from verification, so additional model cost is expected.
  Status reads only calculate pending work; reconciliation remains bounded and resumes normally after writing the new format.
- Unmarked synthetic errors cannot reliably be distinguished from ordinary chat, so online paths retain them; not all historical
  errors are isolated. Main octop-harness/Octop paths raise exceptions; custom hosts synthesizing replies must mark
  `payload.octop_runtime_error=true`. Legacy fixed error text only produces review hints. Missing/mixed evidence yields read-only
  review_*_ids, not new UI tasks or automatic deactivation. Manual saves/approval/edits are protected by provenance, not wording. See ADR-041.

## Storage and maintenance

- Shared PG pool budgets apply only within one process and connection configuration. Reserve additional server capacity for
  other processes, configurations, and host control-plane connections. Long transactions occupy the business pool;
  saturation waits for a bounded time, then errors rather than growing indefinitely. CI/release uses dedicated PG;
  a local environment skipping unavailable services is not PG acceptance.
- `run_gc()` retention currently supports SQLite only; PG returns empty statistics. This is an existing capability gap.
  Row deletion, checkpoint retention, and physical reclamation are different operations; none proves a host schedules them automatically.
- PostgreSQL checkpoint retention requires a caller-verified thread ID. To apply, callers must pause execution,
  resumes and forks for that thread across all hosts. A transaction-level writer reservation cannot see a graph
  that has read a checkpoint but has yet to write. Scheduled retention skips the shared tables. Threads with
  persistent or unrecognized subgraph streams are preserved. Ordinary VACUUM makes deleted space reusable.
  Field deduplication and expansion apply to SQLite files.
- Memory written by 0.9.6 to 0.9.11 sits in PG schema `harness_memory`. A namespace still empty in `octop_memory` is copied on open;
  one that already has new rows is only merged through `Memory.merge_legacy_schema()`, which skips rows whose keys exist and can leave
  similar entities or branches twice. The old schema is never changed or dropped. SQLite never used it and rejects the merge.
  The per-namespace lock does not stop ordinary writes: a new-version writer in another process during the automatic copy ends up
  merged, and 0.9.x writers after the copy are only reported (`legacy_grew`, net growth per table; one-for-one replacement is not
  detected). Dropping the whole `octop_memory` schema loses the migration and purge markers, so old rows would be copied again.
  A merge into a table with a deferrable unique constraint is refused (`unsupported`): `ON CONFLICT` cannot use it.
- The older per-namespace-schema migration (`_migrate_legacy_schema`) relies on the connection's implicit transaction; with
  `autocommit=True` a failure part-way can leave a partial copy. The pre-1.0 shared-schema copy uses an explicit transaction.
- Without PostgreSQL `btree_gin`, indexes fall back to plain GIN. Namespace filtering stays correct but performance isolation weakens.
  Shared checkpoint maintenance needs database-wide scope checks; even ordinary VACUUM cannot promise no lock waits.
- Some SQLite runtimes report `attempt to write a readonly database` during read-only FTS checks.
  Verify engine compatibility rather than skipping integrity checks.

## Data and writes

| Data | Purpose |
|---|---|
| L0 `RawEvent` | Original evidence, filtered by capture/privacy policy |
| L1 `Candidate` | Extracted/manually constructed candidate, evidence, review state |
| L2 `AtomCard` | Canonical fact, provenance, confidence, supersession |
| L2.5 `Episode` / digest | Event memory and periodic summaries |
| L3 `Entity` / `EntityPage` | Entity anchor, consolidated page, headline |
| L4 journal | Business decisions and selected lifecycle records, not every SQL mutation |

```text
capture → RawEvent → extraction → Candidate → promotion → AtomCard → dirty page → regeneration
              └──event extraction──→ Episode                 └────atom_id────→ tree leaf
```

Candidates may promote, merge, drop, or enter conflict/needs_review automatically; not every candidate needs a human.
`Memory.store()` needs no LLM and creates manual RawEvent/Candidate/AtomCard plus a leaf reference.
`Memory.store(kind=...)` and `MemoryService.save(kind=...)` preserve the caller's Fact/Preference/Decision/Task
as Candidate.candidate_type; omission remains Fact. The manual path does not infer a kind or call an LLM.
Topic/entity type remains independent. Non-Fact kinds on directory nodes and ConflictCandidate manual promotion
are rejected before writes; conflict candidates still require the existing review path. Evidence, transaction,
user provenance, and asynchronous review scheduling are preserved. Dashboard kind/filter/statistics already
read the linked candidate. This additive API is unreleased; Harness must load a supporting memory version
before sending typed saves. Existing stored facts are unchanged; Task storage is not reminder scheduling.
`root → branch → leaf` is an organization tree; leaf `atom_id` projects the canonical assertion without a second fact copy.
Manual correction creates a successor, supersedes an active old atom only, and journals `user_edit`, without fabricating conversation evidence.
Absolute event times use aware UTC.

### Extraction and durable progress

`CandidateExtractor` in `pipeline/extractor/__init__.py` has no persistence side effects.
Defaults split at **100 events** and **20,000 estimated characters**: body length plus 200 characters per event,
not a strict serialized-prompt character/token limit. A single oversized event gets its own batch and is not truncated/dropped.
Constructor arguments can override the limits; they are not currently host JSON settings.
Merge candidates, warnings, cap_warning, and llm_calls across batches; the first failed batch stops the pass with `failure_reason`.

Runtime reads at most 10,000 session raw events per call, then excludes extracted IDs.
Backend meta persists `extracted_ids/v1/<session>`; the in-memory LRU holds at most 16 sessions.
Eviction or Runtime reconstruction reloads meta, so progress is not process-local only.
After all model batches succeed, candidates and cursor commit in one backend transaction, then update the in-memory set.
Candidate/strict-cursor write failures roll back together. Model failures do not advance the cursor either;
a later retry reruns this pass's input rather than persisting successful batches individually.

These cursor/transaction guarantees belong to Runtime/Service/Bridge `extract`.
Low-level `extract_session(..., persist=True)` stores returned candidates without an incremental cursor
or rejecting partial candidates carrying `failure_reason`; its failure semantics differ.

Promotion, page regeneration, and Episode extraction follow the candidate/cursor commit, outside that transaction.
The cursor certifies candidate extraction, not every downstream stage. Pending candidates can resume through promote.
Episodes use the same raw input and an independent prompt; their failures are nonfatal enrichment failures.
`extract_run` overwrites `last_extract_run` meta only; it does not append journal rows, and the old heartbeat setting no longer controls writes.

### Manual document governance

MemoryService/Bridge → MemoryRuntime → operations.retention shares one implementation.
Hosts supply current USER.md/MEMORY.md and an optional freshness callback; hosts still own file I/O and session-snapshot loading.
`MemoryService.save()` stores and notifies the nonblocking callback registered with `set_manual_review_scheduler()`;
it does not reconcile synchronously. A host worker/maintenance tick calls synchronous `review_new_memory(max_atoms=20)`
and reads current files through the provider. Missing provider/empty files return `None`. Run model review outside the chat turn.
Explicit `reconcile_manual_documents()` defaults to 100 atoms; total document length is capped at 100,000 characters.

Only high-confidence mutually exclusive facts with explicit subject/scope and valid quotations can atomically
soft-deactivate old atoms and create replacement Candidates/journal entries. Adoption follows review.
Uncertainty/model failure does not force deactivation; partial work can continue.
`manual_documents/v1` stores versions, compared assertion hashes, unresolved work, and audit snapshots;
`manual_documents/recall/v1` stores a small suppression manifest. Full files are not bulk-imported into atoms/FTS.

The audit `uncertain` dictionary tracks inconclusive active assertion hashes; compared is not verified.
Without that dictionary in legacy records, checked progress is untrusted: status reads calculate pending work without mutation;
next reconciliation performs a bounded re-audit and writes the resumable new format.
An explicit empty dictionary is valid resolved state and does not restart review.
Recall deduplicates against the actual session's `manual_context` and suppresses conflicting old-atom raw fallback and stale pages awaiting regeneration.
Adoption checks the last reconciliation version; hosts should supply current `manual_documents` to catch changes not yet reconciled.

### Runtime error isolation

Online capture, Candidate/Episode extraction, promotion, and raw prompt recall exclude errors by structured provenance only,
without intent/troubleshooting-value keyword lists. Agents choose when to call `memory_save`.
Background capture retains length and other policy filters; explicit saving does not inherit the short-message length limit.
Custom hosts synthesizing error replies mark `payload.octop_runtime_error=true`.
Harness owns `on_failure="error"`, checkpoint task errors, and team-turn exclusion;
this is not a promise that memory recognizes every error message by its wording.

`audit_runtime_errors()` previews by default. Apply mode deactivates automatic atoms/rejects unresolved candidates only when
all evidence is marked errors; provenance protects manual saves/approval/edits.
Legacy fixed error text only creates review hints. Missing/mixed provenance returns `review_atom_ids`/`review_candidate_ids`
without changing those records or raw evidence.

### Page regeneration

Dirty state triggers generation; not every write refreshes a page immediately. Regeneration preserves `## My Notes`.
`summary_version` advances on body generation/editing. Storage-managed `mutation_version` advances on body upsert,
dirty invalidation, manual editing, and successful generation. Regeneration ensures a dirty stub, then reads revision/atoms;
model calls hold no database transaction.

Success/failure writebacks compare the snapshot revision in the backend's conditional UPDATE.
A stale result returns `stale_snapshot` or its original failure reason and logs a failure journal,
without changing newer content, dirty state, or failure counts. A current-revision failure updates retry state only,
not mutation_version. Failed conditional writes never fall back to unconditional upsert.
Fact changes use the existing dirty chain; lower-level bypasses receive no additional governance.
SQLite/PG schema 2 adds default-zero revision columns automatically. SQLite checks/adds under `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`;
PG checks under the initialization advisory lock and ALTERs only if missing, avoiding no-op DDL exclusive locks.
Ordinary page apply retains legacy backend signatures; explicit version conditions require a custom backend's conditional parameters and atomic checks.

## Recall and reads

Main pipeline: cache → parse → route → atom-only source restriction → gather → raw policy → rerank → diversify → suppress → budget → render.
`recall_for_prompt(atom_only=True)` is the automatic-injection default, gathering atom and optional vector atom hits only.
No atom match returns empty; raw, page_headline, and episode cannot fill the prompt. Service, Hermes prefetch, and CLI use this default.
Runtime `memory_search` explicitly passes `atom_only=False` for ordinary tools and preserves configurable raw fallback and host Markdown.
OpenClaw hybrid prefetch sends `atomOnly: true`; Runtime then skips non-atom sources and host files. The plugin also filters
host-prefetched/returned results and prompt rendering to canonical atom paths. Explicit tools keep existing sources.
Cache scope includes atom-only mode, raw policy, current session, and manual-document snapshots to prevent cross-mode reuse.
With multi-source retrieval, raw fallback excludes raw when durable results exist rather than topping up the count;
current session/thread scope excludes that conversation's raw. The legacy `recall_multi_source` helper is unchanged.
`memory_get` reads the virtual path returned by search; hosts should not guess IDs.

## Storage and connections

SQLite isolates namespaces with table prefixes; PostgreSQL uses shared `octop_memory` schema and namespace-first keys.
Chroma/Qdrant are optional indexes, not replacements for relational data/transactions; real vector-backend validation is still missing.
LangGraph checkpoints optionally persist execution state; `checkpoint_ns` differs from the memory namespace.
SQLite and PostgreSQL retention select checkpoints by count or age, then keep the ancestry and writes needed by each survivor.
The saver serializes planning and deletion in a single transaction per thread. Only a survivor that can restore
without its deleted parent loses that link. IDs, payloads and pending writes stay intact.
Offline migration honors its caller's explicit `protected_ids` before evaluating replay dependencies.
Harness uses scheduled SQLite cleanup with `skip_pending=True`, leaving checkpoints with pending head work intact.
For root-only threads Harness also supplies its messages reducer. A retained boundary with only a message
dependency can store a full DeltaChannel snapshot in the pruning transaction. The boundary keeps its ID,
metadata and writes. The planner keeps dependencies for other channels and unrecognized checkpoint formats.
PostgreSQL stores the message seed in the native versioned blob table and holds a transaction-level writer
reservation while applying a thread's plan. Consistent PG replay handles a reader that fetched the retained
boundary before it was detached. PostgreSQL releases blob versions only when every surviving checkpoint
in that namespace has stopped referencing them. Retained branches that can reuse an integer message
version keep their replay ancestry.
The PostgreSQL dispatcher requires an explicit caller-verified thread ID and offline confirmation for writes.
Scheduled maintenance has neither an ownership source nor a cross-host pause and skips PG pruning.
Opt-in subgraph removal preserves threads with stable or unrecognized namespaces and checks the reconstructed
root reply when the caller supplies a messages DeltaChannel.

Each SQLite backend has one connection and a reentrant lock across complete SQL/results, transactions, maintenance, and close.
Failed standalone writes roll back; close waits for operations and never reopens. Different backends have independent locks;
checkpoints use a separate connection and transaction. See ADR-039.

PG shares business (8) and checkpoint/maintenance (4) pools by process, normalized DSN, and driver options, not namespace.
Ordinary cursors lease short transactions; explicit transactions hold one connection and backend lock, without reconnecting later writes
in a broken transaction. Pools use `min_size=0`, `max_idle=600`, liveness checks, at most 64 waiters, and a 30-second timeout.
Lease close is idempotent; only the last release closes the pool. Checkpoint DDL initializes once per pool under serialization;
failure releases the lease and permits retry. Maintenance shares the autocommit pool. See ADR-040.

## Host files and migration

`HostFilesIndex` is a separate SQLite file index even with PG memory.
When enabled, it scans MEMORY.md, USER.md, DREAMS.md, date-named `memory/*.md`, and default `topics/*.md`/`projects/*.md`
or an explicit allowlist, not the whole workspace. Only safe relative Markdown globs are accepted;
anchors, hidden paths, and `..` are rejected. Reads use indexed snapshots rather than rereading live files.

Portable agent discovery defaults to `~/.octop/agents/*/memory.sqlite` and `~/.octop-harness/*/memory.sqlite`.

`TEST_POSTGRES_DSN` fails. Without the variable, local tests probe quickly and skip only when unavailable,
avoiding repeated 30-second pool waits across the suite.

After base tests, CI/release installs a pinned octop-harness, checks its real middleware import, and runs integration contracts.
The host is not a production dependency of memory. Missing local host cases may skip but must not be reported as passed.
See `Test real Harness background review` in the [CI workflow](../../.github/workflows/ci.yml) for installation and revision.
After installation, use `--no-sync` to retain host test dependencies and confirm cases did not skip.

`test_postgres_pool.py` verifies at most 12 total business/checkpoint connections for 69 mixed-use instances,
queue saturation/timeouts, idle zero/reconnect, server-closed idle connections, initialization retry,
shared maintenance capacity, and closing one instance without affecting others.
Idle tests shorten reclamation only in the test process; production keeps `max_idle=600`.
Closure tests assert closed leases, zero references, and a closed real pool before bounded polling for remote
`pg_stat_activity` to reach zero; closing a client socket does not imply synchronous server-process exit.
Backend-specific capabilities must explicitly reject the other backend and document limits.
Use tmp_path, never real user memory; report optional-dependency and host-E2E skips separately.
`test_fd_pressure.py` sets soft NOFILE=1024 in a separate POSIX process, exercising 69 temporary Memory instances
with 8 persistent workers and checking socket creation and return to baseline after close.
It does not alter pytest's process limit. Windows/insufficient hard limits skip; report the Linux `/proc` regression separately.
If uv cache is unavailable but the virtual environment is ready, use `make all RUN='.venv/bin/python -m'`.

## Validation across repositories

Run these representative consumer checks from their own repository roots, selected by actual impact;
not every task needs all repositories. Read each repository's AGENTS and prepare its development environment first.
Code commits also run that repository's full gate. Documentation-only maintenance verifies entry points and documents,
without operating running agents or real user data.

Octop memory components have adjacent `*.test.tsx` files. In `dashboard/`, run `npm test -- src/pages/Agent/Memory`
or the affected individual file, plus `npx tsc -b` and `make build-frontend` according to that repository's rules.
Display-only work needs no new business implementation in memory/Harness.

Integration cases must load the changed versions: record each source revision/resolved dependency and check import origins.
Passing with an old installed host dependency does not validate new source. `--no-sync` preserves an already prepared environment;
it does not install the intended sources or verify versions. This repository's fixed CI host covers its listed contracts,
not all future host versions. Model responses may be mocked; do not replace entire Service/Middleware/configuration-forwarding
or acceptance-critical backend paths with stubs. Schema/persistence integration uses real dedicated PG and covers legacy upgrades,
namespace isolation, and consumer reopening/restoration.

## Validation boundaries

Portable discovery tests isolate home expansion to tmp_path, covering current agent paths and explicit extra_paths.
Dry runs use temporary destination databases and compare before/after data. Recall degradation/page-headline tests also use temporary stores,
not the default user database.

Documentation tests check local links, public text, and layout contracts, not the absence of every possible secret.
Host installation, optional dependencies, real PG, and recall quality need separate validation.
See [modifying adapters](../integrations.md#modifying-adapters) for OpenClaw/Hermes plugin checks and real-host E2E scripts.
Without an installed host/executed script, do not claim E2E acceptance. Vector cases currently use fake/mock clients, not real services.
The synthetic evaluator's historical `P@5` denominator is the number of returned top-five items, not a fixed five;
MRR uses the complete returned list. The small corpus favors entity queries; dates/IDs vary per run.
Defaults compare raw_fts and full_pipeline, and exit status reflects only the configured delta gate.
Evaluation is outside `make all`/CI and does not establish production recall quality.
Comment-only maintenance must not alter metric definitions or seed data.

# 给 AI 的接入说明（把这一页 + token 交给 AI 即可）

你要做的是：把用户这台机器上的编码终端接到 octop-memory。**只需要两个输入**：

- `OCTOP_URL`：MCP 地址，形如 `https://<octop-host>/mcp/memory/`（本地实例是 `http://127.0.0.1:8088/mcp/memory/`）
- `OCTOP_TOKEN`：用户级 MCP token，形如 `omcp_…`（用户在 Octop「个性化 → 记忆 → 终端接入」创建）

## 规则（必须遵守）

1. 不要把 token 写进任何仓库、脚本文件或提交里；只通过命令行参数/环境变量传给安装器
2. 不要 `echo`/打印 token，也不要写进日志
3. 安装器会写 `~/.claude/hooks-events/config.json` 等文件（权限 0600），不要把它复制进项目目录
4. 只运行下面与当前系统对应的命令；不要自己改 hook 配置或手写 `settings.json`

## macOS / Linux

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TencentCloud/octop-memory/main/plugins/harness/install.sh \
  | sh -s -- --url "$OCTOP_URL" --token "$OCTOP_TOKEN"
```

或从本地仓库：`sh plugins/harness/install.sh --url "$OCTOP_URL" --token "$OCTOP_TOKEN"`

- 只装部分终端：追加 `--terminals claude-code,codex`
- 装到某个项目：追加 `--project "$PWD"`

依赖：`uvx`（推荐）或 `pipx` 或 `python3`（脚本会用临时 venv 装安装器）。

## Windows

```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TencentCloud/octop-memory/main/plugins/harness/install.ps1 -OutFile install.ps1
.\install.ps1 -Url $env:OCTOP_URL -Token $env:OCTOP_TOKEN
```

依赖：`uvx` / `pipx` / `python`（脚本会用 `%TEMP%` 下的临时 venv）。

## 验证（AI 自己做完要报告结果）

```sh
# 召回日志：应出现 hits=N http=200
tail -n 5 ~/.claude/hooks-events/octop-hook.log    # macOS/Linux
# Windows: Get-Content $env:USERPROFILE\.claude\hooks-events\octop-hook.log -Tail 5
```

- 让用户重开终端 / IDE（Codex 首次需要在 Codex 里 trust hook；DSH 需要重启）
- 让用户问一句话，然后在 Octop「终端接入」页看 token 的「接入端」是否出现对应客户端
- 若日志是 401：token 无效/被吊销；403：该接入端被禁用；404：服务端没开 `OCTOP_MEMORY_MCP_ENABLED`

## 卸载

```sh
sh plugins/harness/uninstall.sh [--terminals a,b] [--project <dir>]
# Windows: .\uninstall.ps1 -Terminals a,b
```

## 完成后向用户汇报

- 安装了哪些终端
- 是否通过验证（召回/上报日志）
- 任何需要用户手动做的步骤（重启 IDE、Codex trust hook、DSH 重启）
